newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed market firms amid crop losses.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed market firms amid crop losses.

text.p: Rapeseed prices in northern Europe firmed amid tightening supply from a sharply lower domestic harvest, brokers said.
Traders said the firmer trend should last and raised their seed bids at the farmgate and gatherer level, helped by the impression of farmer hoarding.
They saw support from a higher Chicago soycomplex which rose on Chinese meal buying and dry U.S. weather.
They also cited export demand for German seed from Poland and Scandinavia.
But largely passive crushers refused to follow the trend, citing slow demand for rape and sun oil and meal in Europe itself. They bought very litte, despite underlying demand.
Farm sources said harvesting of remaining rapeseed in the south was interrupted by rain but was progressing well in northern and eastern Germany.
The Bonn farm ministry on Thursday said Germany would widen its role as a net importer of rapeseed as its domestic crop would decline by a third.
It predicted a two million tonne 1996 crop versus 3.1 million tonnes last year, with average yields forecast at just 2.27 tonnes per hectares versus 3.19 in 1995.
This was well below trade forecasts for a 2.5-2.6 million tonne crop.
Trade buyers in the north offered 457.50 marks for spot seed, five marks more than a week ago and 15 marks up from late July levels.
Fob Baltic prices were at 455 marks, up five, basis 3,000 tonne shipments.
Rapeseed buyers at points other than Hamburg were offered at steady prices for September while French September rapeseed fob Moselle was offered at 1,540 francs, ten more than last week.
The November position on the Paris Matif futures exchange last traded seven marks above last night's close at 462 marks.
Local rape meal sellers quoted Sept/October (34 percent protein) little changed at 27.50-27.75 marks/100 kg while Nov/Jan was up 0.50 on the week at 28.75 marks.
Spot soymeal cost 43.25 marks (44 percent protein).
Sept/Oct rape oil was at 85.50 marks/100 kg, versus 83.25 Sept last week when Oct cost 84.50. Nov-Jan oil rose 1.25 marks to 87.75.
